extracted.intended_audience: importers/exporters, trade counsel, interested parties in antidumping administrative reviews, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, and Department of Commerce staff
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register notice announcing a court decision 'not in harmony' with Commerce's administrative review results and publishing amended final results (exporter-specific margins), cash-deposit instructions, and liquidation/assessment guidance. Targets parties affected by an antidumping duty administrative review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timken notice and suspension requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: In its decision in Timken, as clarified by Diamond Sawblades, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit held that, pursuant to section 516A(c) and (e) of the Tariff Act of 1930, as amended (the Act), Commerce must publish a notice of court decision that is not 'in harmony' with a Commerce determination and must suspend liquidation of entries pending a 'conclusive' court decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CIT's April 14, 2025, judgment constitutes a final decision of the CIT that is not in harmony with Commerce's Final Results. Thus, this notice is published in fulfillment of the publication requirements of Timken. (References: Timken Co. v. United States, 893 F.2d 337 (Fed. Cir. 1990); Diamond Sawblades Manufacturers Coalition v. United States, 626 F.3d 1374 (Fed. Cir. 2010); statutory basis: sections 516A(c) and (e) of the Act.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of Final Results following final court judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Because there is now a final court judgment, Commerce is amending its Final Results and with respect to Trina as follows: [Exporter listed] — Weighted-average dumping margin (percent): 9.09.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a court issues a final judgment not in harmony with Commerce's Final Results, Commerce will publish amended final results reflecting the court-mandated changes to exporter-specific weighted-average dumping margins (and will provide the amended margin(s) in the notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Revised cash deposit requirements when no superseding rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Because Trina does not have a superseding cash deposit rate, i.e., there have been no final results published in a subsequent administrative review covering Trina, Commerce will issue revised cash deposit instructions for Trina to U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP). Commerce will revise Trina's cash deposit rate from 10.50 percent to 9.09 percent ad valorem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an exporter lacks a superseding cash deposit rate (no later administrative review final results), Commerce revises the exporter's cash deposit rate and issues instructions to CBP reflecting the amended ad valorem rate derived from the amended final results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liquidation stays under injunction during pendency of appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce remains enjoined by CIT order from liquidating entries that were exported by Trina and were entered, or withdrawn from warehouse, for consumption during the period February 1, 2021, through January 31, 2022. These entries will remain enjoined pursuant to the terms of the injunction during the pendency of any appeals process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An injunction from the court prevents Commerce (and CBP) from liquidating the affected entries while the injunction is in effect. The entries remain suspended until the injunction is lifted or a conclusive court decision is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to CBP to assess antidumping duties per 19 CFR 351.212(b)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event the CIT's ruling is not appealed, or, if appealed, upheld by a final and conclusive court decision, Commerce intends to instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on unliquidated entries of subject merchandise exported by Trina in accordance with 19 CFR 351.212(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commerce will direct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate unliquidated entries covered by the review once the court decision is final and conclusive, following the assessment procedures set out in 19 CFR 351.212(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment/liquidation exception for zero or de minimis importer-specific rates
rubrics_metrics.description: We will instruct CBP to assess antidumping duties on all appropriate entries covered by this review when the importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate is not zero or de minimis. Where an import-specific ad valorem assessment rate is zero or de minimis, we will instruct CBP to liquidate the appropriate entries without regard to antidumping duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the importer-specific ad valorem assessment rate equals zero or is de minimis, Commerce's instruction will be to liquidate entries without applying antidumping duties; otherwise, assess duties. (Reference cited: 19 CFR 351.106(c)(2) for de minimis handling.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Commerce compliance with court remand regarding countervailing-duty adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: The CIT remanded the Final Results to Commerce to further explain or reconsider its decision not to adjust the prices of Trina's sales of subject merchandise during the POR by the countervailing duties imposed on certain programs in the 2017 administrative review of the companion countervailing duty order. In its final results of redetermination, issued on December 18, 2024, Commerce, under respectful protest, adjusted the prices of Trina's sales of subject merchandise during the POR by the countervailing duties imposed on three of the six subsidy programs at issue. On April 14, 2025, the CIT sustained Commerce's final remand redetermination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a court remands Commerce's Final Results, Commerce must further explain or reconsider contested determinations (e.g., whether to adjust sales prices by previously imposed countervailing duties). Commerce may carry out adjustments on remand (sometimes 'under respectful protest'), and the court may sustain or remand further; Commerce's remand redetermination becomes the basis for amended results if sustained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for issuance of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice is issued and published in accordance with sections 516A(c) and (e) and 777(i)(1) of the Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The publication of notices of court decisions not in harmony with Commerce determinations and related actions (e.g., amendment of Final Results, instruction to CBP) are grounded in the cited statutory provisions; parties should refer to these sections for statutory requirements and scope.
